thread:
maya: Hey team — draft for the benchmark outbound script and sales playbook. Main goal: a tight latency + cost narrative that SDRs can use, plus two chart hooks for the website/webinar. Please skim and drop quick asks.

jon: Quick note — please don't lock in exact numbers in copy until eng signs off. Use placeholders for now.

maya: Good call. I've put placeholders like <P50_LATENCY> and <COST_PER_1K>. Also added subject A/B for emails below.

sergio: I can mock two chart layouts: 1) single-panel "latency vs unit cost" scatter with callouts, 2) stacked bars showing cost per 1k tokens across slices. Suggest we emphasize p95 callouts.

elaine: For outbound we need 3 things: cold email, LinkedIn message, and a one-line call opener. Plus a short objection script when they say "we run our own infra."

maya: Pasting current drafts (subject lines + email body). Please comment inline.

maya: ```Subject A: See how Redwood cuts per-token cost without slowing responses
Subject B: Cut inference cost 2x — keep the same latency

Email body:
Hi {{first_name}},
Quick note — we ran a benchmark on common instruction workloads and saw ~2x improvement in per-token spend at equivalent p95 latency. Would love to share a short chart for your workload and two recommendations your infra team can try.

CTA: "Share a quick chart" or "Book 10-min demo"

One-liner to use on call: "We route requests to lower-cost model variants while preserving latency SLOs — no app changes needed."
```

alex: I like Subject B. For outbound, lower friction CTA = "share a quick chart".

elaine: Agreed — chart is less commitment than a demo.

jon: Engine/infra check — recommended columns for the chart CSV: model, workload_slice, p50_ms, p95_ms, cost_per_1k_tokens, batch_size. Also add a column for "routing_variant" if we show fallback behavior.

jon: I can provide provisional numbers but will confirm with infra before marketing materials go live. For an example: p50 ~ 20ms, p95 ~ 120ms on a representative conversational slice, cost_per_1k_tokens depends on quantization and batching — I'll supply a small table.

sergio: Cool. For visuals: use a single accent color for Redwood (green) and muted gray for baseline. Add callout labels for the slices that matter to product teams (short prompts, long instructions, embeddings).

maya: Also want a 1-line hero variant for the site. Options: 
- "Predictable latency. Lower unit economics."
- "Same outputs. Lower cost. Predictable latency at scale."
Thoughts?

elaine: Short is better. I like "Same outputs. Lower cost." as a hero and then a subhead with latency.

alex: SDR request — we need a 1-sentence rebuttal for "we run our own infra."

maya: Draft rebuttal: "Totally — Redwood focuses on sustained inference economics and routing logic that combines model variants, caching, and batching; share a trace and we’ll show a side-by-side in 10 minutes."

jon: I will validate the benchmark numbers and post an "approved stats" comment here by EOD.

maya: Timeline: mock charts + subject A/B + 3 SDR templates by tomorrow AM. @sergio @elaine @alex any last asks?

sergio: I’ll add p95 annotations and a compact legend.

elaine: I’ll write the 3 outbound templates and the objections doc.

alex: I’ll run an A/B in Outreach with Subject B vs Subject A and CTA = "share a quick chart".

maya: :thumbsup: thanks all. I’ll drop the final copy into the marketing drive and link it here once jon confirms numbers.
